perspective:
From Jose Castillo’s perspective:

- I work with Patricia at the community bank, where I sometimes help with maintenance and repairs. We’re friendly and professional, and we usually chat about our day-to-day work.
- Recently, I noticed Patricia seemed more withdrawn than usual. I remembered her as usually vibrant, so I became concerned something might be troubling her.
- I asked her if she was okay. She told me it was “nothing really,” just “some personal stuff,” and thanked me for asking.
- I offered to listen if she ever wanted to talk. She said she appreciated that and that it meant a lot.
- During a lunch break, I overheard her on the phone sounding worried about bills and financial commitments.
- I mentioned that managing finances can be stressful and that I had been reading about financial planning strategies. I offered to discuss them sometime.
- She said that could be helpful and that she had been feeling overwhelmed with her bills lately.
- I offered to look over budgeting tips with her and told her to let me know when she felt up to it. She thanked me and said she’d take me up on it soon.
- Later, I worried I might have overstepped by bringing up finances. I checked in with her and clarified that I wanted to help, not pry.
- She told me she didn’t think I was prying and that she was actually grateful for the offer.
- I told her I respected her privacy and just wanted to support her as a friend. She said she really appreciated that and that it was good to know she had someone to turn to.
- After that, I sensed she appreciated my concern but might prefer to handle things privately, so I tried to keep my support light.
- I continued checking in with her at work, keeping the tone friendly and supportive. I offered help, even just for coffee, and she said she was handling things and really appreciated my support.
